page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-oriented instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 vCPUs backed by 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, along with 16 GB of RAM, yielding a 4 GB memory allocation per vCPU. It utilizes dedicated CPU allocation with 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server includes hardware instruction support for AES cryptography, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, and BMI2, but lacks attached GPUs and bundled local storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top quartile for stress-ng single-thread tests. However, overall multi-core performance sits in the lower quartile across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark suites due to the physical core count limitation. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth remain in the middle category, as do single-threaded text processing and AES encryption benchmarks. Multi-threaded operations, including software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET throughput, perform in lower benchmark percentiles.

From a resource and cost efficiency perspective, c2d-standard-4 provides dedicated x86 execution for tasks reliant on single-thread execution speed without requiring large memory pools or hardware acceleration. Because local storage is absent, disk IO relies entirely on attached block storage volumes. This instance profile is suited for light web serving, single-threaded batch processing, lightweight API endpoints, and microservices that benefit from predictable AMD EPYC core performance.
